title: Group medical visits versus individual reviews for adults with type 2 diabetes in general practice: protocol for an individually randomised, partially nested trial
abstract: Objective: to compare HbA1c at 12 months between adults with type 2 diabetes offered group medical visits and those continuing individual reviews. Design: individually randomised, partially nested trial across several general practices. Participants: adults with HbA1c of 58 mmol/mol or more. Results will be reported after follow-up.
introduction: Group medical visits lower HbA1c modestly in trials, but a general practice trial was imprecise, and comparisons of attenders with non-attenders are confounded by self-selection.
methods: Consenting patients are randomised 1:1 by a remote system, stratified by practice and baseline HbA1c. The primary outcome is laboratory HbA1c at 12 months, analysed with a linear mixed model with a random effect for group in the intervention arm.
results: No patients have been recruited yet. The report will present recruitment, attendance, HbA1c and distress by arm, and hypoglycaemia.
discussion: The discussion will interpret the effect against the pooled estimate, attendance and equity, and state what the result means for expanding group visits.
limitations: Unblinded delivery, possible contamination, and reliance on neighbouring practices for recruitment.
conclusion: To be written after the trial.
reportingChecklist: SPIRIT 2013 for the protocol; CONSORT 2010 with the non-pharmacological extension for the results
summary: Protocol-style draft with results left empty.
